response.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(l.WBC) AS avg_wbc, AVG(l.HGB / l.HCT) AS ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), with_mean AS (SELECT ID, SEX, avg_wbc, ratio, AVG(ratio) OVER () AS mean_ratio FROM per_patient) SELECT ID, SEX, avg_wbc, ratio, ratio - mean_ratio AS gap FROM with_mean WHERE ratio > mean_ratio ORDER BY gap DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: A patient's ratio is the average of the per-record HGB/HCT values, skipping records where either is missing (or HCT is 0, which yields NULL in SQLite). It is not AVG(HGB)/AVG(HCT).

The 'mean of that ratio across all patients' is the average of the per-patient ratios, so each patient counts equally regardless of how many lab records they have. Patients with a NULL ratio are excluded from that mean.
Patients with a NULL ratio fail the > filter, so they are dropped. The 'missing values last' ordering therefore has no effect.

alternatives.interpretation: The comparison mean is the average HGB/HCT over all joined lab records (each record weighted equally) rather than the average of per-patient ratios.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(l.WBC) AS avg_wbc, AVG(l.HGB / l.HCT) AS ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), overall AS (SELECT AVG(l.HGB / l.HCT) AS mean_ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID) SELECT pp.ID, pp.SEX, pp.avg_wbc, pp.ratio, pp.ratio - o.mean_ratio AS gap FROM per_patient pp CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE pp.ratio > o.mean_ratio ORDER BY gap DESC LIMIT 10
